obligations.note: is_allowed now returns true for any report:<action> whenever (role, <action>) is in GRANTS, so pairs such as (treasury_manager, report:release_payment) and (payments_officer, report:approve_payment) are granted even though they are not explicit entries in controls/payments/access-policy.json. The passing matrix test only checks the declared GRANTS tuples and does not cover this alias, so the grants no longer equal the approved default-deny policy.

The auditor's grants remain view_account, view_audit, view_reports, and export_ledger, none of which are in STATE_CHANGING, and the report: prefix only rechecks those same grants. The exhaustive test_auditor_is_read_only passed unskipped on the head commit.

it_admin is still granted only manage_users, rotate_keys, purge_npi, and view_audit, so report:approve_payment and report:release_payment stay denied. The exhaustive test_it_admin_cannot_approve_or_release passed on the head commit.
The change names ticket CHG-25503, which Erik Brandt (change_manager) approved on 2026-10-01 before review, and its component payments.access matches the only touched file, rbac.py.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author Sofia Santos, approved a code_review of commit 6256a35b.
The change is a single commit and both the code_review and security_review name that head commit, so the approvals cover what would be merged.

records/ci/run.json shows ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments succeeded on 6256a35b, and the JUnit report has 172 tests with 0 failures, errors, or skips, including the registered ACC-1, ACC-2, and SOD-1 control tests.
rbac.py is security_sensitive (payments.access), and Ines Halvorsen, a security_reviewer who is not the author, approved a security_review of the head commit.
The only changed path is apps/baseline-payments/payments/rbac.py, which is not under the protected controls, control-test, or CI paths, so a control_owner approval is not required.

The report: alias is a deviation from ACC-1 on payments.access, and the register has no approved unexpired exception for that obligation and component. EXC-0141 expired on 2026-09-06, before the 2026-10-06 review time.
No acceptance-ledger cover (payments.py, audit.py, routes.py, or the mortgage files) is modified, so those earlier entries have not lapsed; they also do not evidence the new rbac behavior.

summary: The change adds a report: prefix in payments is_allowed that treats report:<action> as the underlying grant. That admits role-action pairs that are not in the approved access policy, including report:approve_payment and report:release_payment, so ACC-1 is violated and no valid exception covers it. Ticket, independent approvals, security review, and a green full-suite run on the head commit are in order, and the auditor and IT-admin restrictions still hold for their real grants, but the access-matrix deviation blocks acceptance.
